points.description: Conclusion that identifies the ranking or extremes supported by the data: plastic B stretched the most (about 22-23 mm) and plastic A the least (about 10-12 mm); C and D are in between (D about 20 mm, C about 13-14 mm). Must be consistent with the data. Stating B is the most stretchable and A the least earns full marks. Correct ranking B > D > C > A also earns full marks.

levels.says: Names only the most stretchy or the least stretchy plastic correctly, or gives a vague correct comparison without naming plastics (e.g. 'plastics differ in stretchiness'), or cites values with no conclusion.

points.description: First valid improvement to the experimental design or validity, stated specifically (e.g. more trials and averaging; control sample dimensions such as length, width, thickness; use identical mass on each sample; use more samples per plastic type; more precise measuring; consistent hang time or temperature). Must be something not already done (two trials and a five-minute hang time alone do not count).

Second valid improvement, different in idea from P2, stated specifically (from the list in P2 or another correct design/validity improvement). Do not award if it repeats P2 in different wording. Vague answers like 'be more careful' or 'do it better' earn nothing.

rubric.notes: Full marks: a data-supported conclusion (B most stretch, A least) plus two distinct, specific, valid improvements. Part marks only on the conclusion for incomplete statements. No marks for vague improvements or for repeating the same improvement twice.
rubric.answer_key:
Conclusion: Plastic B stretched the most (22 and 23 mm, mean 22.5 mm), then D (20 mm), C (13.5 mm), and A the least (mean 11 mm). So B is the most stretchable and A the least. Results were fairly consistent between trials (D identical, small differences for others).
Improvements (any two): use more trials/repeats and average; use samples of identical size (length, width, thickness) as the starting size; use the same mass/weights on every sample and state it; use a control/ensure the same hanging time and temperature; measure more precisely (ruler with finer scale, or measure while hanging); test more samples of each plastic type; allow the plastic time to recover before measuring or measure at a consistent time; test a wider range of weights.

review_notes: P1 contradicts itself: the main text says a conclusion with no reference to the data earns 0, but the partial level gives half marks for naming B or A without data.
P2 and P3 list 'more trials/repeats' and 'larger sample size/more samples' as separate examples, so one idea (more repeats) could be rewarded twice; they should count as one improvement.

P2 and P3 require the improvement to be 'linked to why it helps', which is not in the question and makes the point hard to check; a clear, specific improvement should be enough, with a reason only needed where the change is otherwise unclear.
